newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond vols steady despite weak bonds.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond vols steady despite weak bonds.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. T-bond options were little changed, despite the weakness in bond prices and several event risks later in the week including Friday's February employment report, traders said.

"What we're seeing is volatility correct itself before the employment report instead of having that huge drop-off right after the number," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT).
Implied volatilities for April and June T-bond futures options were barely changed from Monday at around 10.1 percent and 10.0 percent respectively.
Traders said the market appeared to be discounting any surprises from the second leg of Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins testimony on Wednesday.
"Everything he's going to say to move the market, he's already said," the brokerage trader noted. "And he, as well as the rest of us, won't know what the payrolls are going to be until Friday."

June T-bond futures slid below 110-00 to a low of 109-25/32 in late trade after a stronger-than-expected 2.4 percent rise in Redbook retail sales index. But traders said the selloff was modest and volatilities barely reacted.
There were few big option trades in the CBOT bond pit today as most traders refrained from taking huge positions ahead of the Greenspan testimony.

Among the largest deals, an investment bank bought 1,000 contracts of June 108 puts and sold 1,000 April 111 puts in a so-called "diagonal" spread. Another investment bank was seen buying 2,000 legs of June 108-110 put spread.
Many traders expected the Fed to tighten credit at its Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting in May if it does not do so at the March 25 FOMC meeting.

But they added that interest rate market could see a modest rebound, even if it was just a modest corrective bounce, if the payrolls and hourly earnings figures in Friday's jobs data were not too strong.
"It is getting oversold a bit, although it's difficult to say how much bounce the market's got in it," a Eurodollar trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) said.

Implied volatilities for June and September Eurodollar futures options were little changed, at around 10.5 and 14.2 percent respectively, as underlying futures ended marginally softer, shedding early gains.
